Reference / template/engine

template/engine#

Templates over JSON: one small language, compiled once, rendered as text.

Version: v1.0.0

Synopsis#

let greeting = Template("Hello, {{user.name}}! You have {{user.unread}} new messages.");
greeting.string(ParsedJson(text).root());
greeting.write(data: data, destination: Stdout());

let order = Template("Order {{id}}:\n{{#items}}  - {{title}}\n{{/items}}{{^items}}  (empty)\n{{/items}}");

Description#

Templates over JSON: one small language, compiled once, rendered as text.

The language (Mustache's core, nothing more):

  • {{path}} is a value: a dotted path of members (user.name) read from the current context, or {{.}}, the context itself;
  • {{#path}}…{{/path}} is a section and {{^path}}…{{/path}} an inverted one;
  • {{! comment }} is dropped; {{{{ and }}}} write {{ and }};
  • a tag alone on its line takes its indentation and line end with it. There are no expressions, filters, functions or assignments.

Values. A string is written as it is, a number in its canonical form (12.5), a boolean as true or false, null as nothing. An object or an array as a value is NonScalarTemplateValue; a member that is not there is MissingTemplateValue. Names are read from the current context only, not from the contexts around it.

Sections. A section on an array renders once per item, the item as the context; on an object, once with the object as the context; on true, a number or a non-empty string, once with that value as the context; on false, null, "", [] or a missing member, not at all. An inverted section renders once, in the enclosing context, exactly when the section would not render; for an object it never does.

Compiling. The source is parsed and checked whole on the first render and kept: rendering again reuses it, and rendering never changes it. A source that is not a template is TemplateFailure, with its line and column, before anything is written. write() sends the output piece by piece; what was written before a failure (a missing value, a limit) stays written.

Limits (TemplateLimits): the source's characters, its tokens, how deep sections nest, how many section bodies render, the output's UTF-8 bytes and the members of an object read on a path. Going past one is its own error.

object TemplatePartials#

object TemplatePartials

Named sources a template includes with {{>name}}, in the template's own mode and with its data and limits.

Template(source: "{{#items}}{{>item}}{{/items}}", partials: TemplatePartials(["item": "- {{title}}\n"]));

Names are exact, without trimming or case folding, and a map has each name once. Only the partials a template reaches are compiled, each once, before anything is written; one it reaches and the library lacks is TemplateError.partial(name). A partial may include itself: TemplateLimits bounds how deep partials nest and how many render.
